about: Rules the Meta Ads agent uses to check ad text against Meta's Advertising Standards. Each rule has an id, a level (BLOCK = fix before running, WARN = check it), the section of policies/meta-advertising-standards.md it comes from, a plain explanation and a rewrite hint. Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions, matched case-insensitively unless the rule sets flags. To add a rule, copy one, give it a new id, and run: node src/index.js policy rules

rules.title: Says the reader has a health condition
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that say or hint that the reader has a health condition. "You" or "your" next to a condition reads as if you know their private health details.
rules.rewrite: Talk about the service, not the reader. Example: "Anxiety support classes, Tuesday evenings" instead of "Are you struggling with anxiety?"

rules.title: Says the reader has money trouble
attributes: \b(in debt|debts?|bad credit|poor credit|low credit|credit score|broke|bankrupt(cy)?|low[- ]income|can'?t pay|cannot afford|can'?t afford|behind on (bills|rent|payments)|unemployed|out of work|struggling financially)\b
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that imply the reader is in debt, broke or has bad credit.
rules.rewrite: Describe the help you offer. Example: "Debt planning sessions for small business owners" instead of "Drowning in your debt?"

rules.title: Says how old the reader is
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that say or hint at the reader's age, such as "Are you over 50?".
rules.rewrite: Name the group without "you". Example: "Strength classes designed for people over 50".

rules.title: Says what the reader believes
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that say or hint at the reader's religion, such as "Are you Christian?".
rules.rewrite: Describe the offer for the group. Example: "A Christian book club meeting on Sundays".

rules.title: Says the reader's sexual orientation or gender identity
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that say or hint at the reader's sexual orientation or gender identity.
rules.rewrite: Describe the community or event instead. Example: "LGBTQ+ founders meetup, first Friday of the month".

rules.title: Says the reader's race or ethnicity
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that say or hint at the reader's race or ethnicity.
rules.rewrite: Describe the offer for the community without "you". Example: "Grants for Latina-owned small businesses".

rules.title: Says the reader has a criminal record
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that say or hint that the reader has been arrested or convicted.
rules.rewrite: Describe the service. Example: "Record expungement help, free first call".

rules.title: Promises a guaranteed result
rules.explain: Meta treats promised results as misleading because no one can guarantee how a person will respond. A money-back guarantee is fine; a results guarantee is not.
rules.rewrite: Say what people get, not what is guaranteed. Example: "Join a 7-day guided breathing course" instead of "Feel better in 7 days, guaranteed".

rules.title: Promises results within a short time
rules.explain: A short time frame next to a result (feel better, lose weight, earn) can read as an unrealistic promise. Fine for a course length or a delivery time.
rules.rewrite: Make the time about the offer, not the outcome. Example: "A 7-day course" instead of "Feel better in 7 days".

rules.section: 3. Guaranteed or unrealistic results, income claims
rules.title: Promises income or quick money
rules.explain: Meta rejects income promises and get-rich-quick claims as deceptive.
rules.rewrite: Describe the skill or service. Example: "Learn how to price your services, 4-week course" instead of "Make $10,000 a month from home".

rules.section: 3. Guaranteed or unrealistic results, income claims
rules.title: Promises investment returns
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that promise investment returns or say an investment has no risk.
rules.rewrite: Explain what the product is and link to the risks. Example: "See how our managed fund works".

rules.title: Pushes the reader with time pressure
patterns: \b(hurry|act (now|fast)|last chance|limited time( only)?|ends (tonight|today|at midnight|soon)|only \d+ (spots?|seats?|places?|left|remaining)|(spots?|seats?) (are )?(filling|going) fast|before it'?s too late|don'?t miss out|today only|while (stocks?|supplies) last|expires (tonight|today|in \d+ (hours?|minutes?)))\b
rules.explain: Real deadlines are fine. Fake or repeating ones are deceptive, and pressure words can make Meta show the ad less.
rules.rewrite: Give the real date. Example: "Enrolment closes 15 October" instead of "Hurry, ends tonight!"

rules.section: 2. Health and wellness claims, before/after images
rules.title: Mentions before and after results
rules.explain: Before/after images are a common rejection for weight loss, fitness and skincare. They are only allowed for some cosmetic procedures, shown to people 18 and over.
rules.rewrite: Use one photo of the product in real use, or a customer's words. Example: "Here is what Sarah said after her third session".

rules.section: 2. Health and wellness claims, body image
rules.title: Makes people feel bad about their body
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that shame people about how they look or point at body parts negatively.
rules.rewrite: Speak to the goal, not the flaw. Example: "Feel strong with three short workouts a week".

rules.title: Claims to cure a disease
rules.explain: Meta rejects claims to cure diseases, especially ones without a known cure.
rules.rewrite: Describe the support you offer. Example: "Nutrition coaching for people managing diabetes".

rules.title: Weight loss claim
rules.explain: Weight loss ads must target 18+ only, state a realistic time frame and avoid miracle claims.
rules.rewrite: Lead with the routine, not the number. Example: "A 12-week coached plan for healthy eating". Set the ad set to 18+.

rules.title: Clickbait or sensational wording
patterns: \b(you won'?t believe|shocking|doctors hate|one (weird|simple|strange) trick|they don'?t want you to know|jaw[- ]dropping|mind[- ]blowing|what happens next|this changes everything)\b
rules.explain: Meta rejects or limits ads that use sensational language to bait clicks.
rules.rewrite: Say plainly what the person will find. Example: "See the 3-step method we use with clients".

rules.title: Claim that needs proof
patterns: (#\s?1\b|\bnumber one\b|\bbest in the (world|country|industry)\b|\bclinically (proven|tested)\b|\bscientifically proven\b|\bdoctor[- ]recommended\b|\bfda[- ]approved\b|\bno side effects\b|\b100% (safe|natural)\b)
rules.explain: Superlatives and medical or scientific claims must be true and provable, with the proof on the landing page.
rules.rewrite: Keep only what you can prove and say where it comes from. Example: "Rated 4.9 by 212 customers on Google".

rules.title: Fake prize or fake button
patterns: \b(you'?ve (won|been selected)|congratulations,? you|claim your (prize|reward)|click (play|the play button)|tap to unlock|you are the \d+(st|nd|rd|th) visitor)\b
rules.explain: Meta rejects fake prizes, fake buttons and wording that tricks people into clicking.
rules.rewrite: State the real offer. Example: "Get 20% off your first order".

rules.title: Profanity
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads with profanity, even mild or partly hidden.
rules.rewrite: Use a plain word with the same energy. Example: "Stop wasting hours on admin".

rules.title: Shouting: all caps or piles of punctuation
rules.explain: Ads in ALL CAPS or with !!! look like spam and get shown less.
rules.rewrite: Write in normal sentence case with one exclamation mark at most.

rules.title: Asks for sensitive personal data
patterns: \b(social security( number)?|ssn|passport number|bank account (number|details)|credit card (number|details)|card number|password|pin code|medical history|criminal history)\b
rules.explain: Lead forms and ads must not ask for ID numbers, bank or card details, passwords, health or criminal history without Meta's permission.
rules.rewrite: Ask only for name, email and phone, and collect anything sensitive later, securely.

rules.title: Uses a crisis or disaster to sell
rules.explain: Meta rejects ads that use a crisis, disaster or tragedy for commercial gain.
rules.rewrite: Remove the crisis reference and sell on the offer itself.

rules.title: Supplements or weight loss products
rules.explain: Supplements and weight loss products are allowed only for people 18 and over, with no miracle claims.
rules.rewrite: Set the ad set to 18+ and describe the product plainly. Example: "Daily vitamin D, 60 capsules".

rules.title: Alcohol
rules.explain: Alcohol ads must follow local law and target people of legal drinking age (18+ at least).
rules.rewrite: Set the ad set age to your country's legal drinking age and avoid linking drinking to success or health.

rules.title: Dating
rules.explain: Dating ads need Meta's written permission first.
rules.rewrite: Apply for dating ad permission in Business Help before running this.

rules.title: Gambling
rules.explain: Gambling ads need Meta's written permission and 18+ targeting.
rules.rewrite: Apply for gambling ad permission before running this, or remove the gambling reference.

rules.title: Crypto or trading
rules.explain: Crypto trading, exchanges and similar products need Meta's written permission.
rules.rewrite: Apply for crypto ad permission before running this, or remove the reference.

rules.title: Drugs, pharmacy or addiction treatment
rules.explain: Prescription drugs, pharmacies, cannabis and addiction treatment need certification (for example LegitScript) or are not allowed.
rules.rewrite: Check the certification you need before running this, or remove the reference.

rules.title: Tobacco, vapes or nicotine
rules.explain: Meta does not allow ads for tobacco, vapes or nicotine products.
rules.rewrite: Remove the product. Quit-smoking programmes may be allowed if they do not show the product.

rules.title: Weapons, ammunition or explosives
rules.explain: Meta does not allow ads that sell weapons, ammunition or explosives.
rules.rewrite: Remove the weapon reference. Safety training courses may be allowed if they sell no weapons.

rules.title: Payday loans or other banned money products
patterns: \b(payday loans?|cash advance|paycheck advance|binary options?|bail bonds?|short[- ]term loans?)\b
rules.explain: Meta does not allow payday loans, short-term loans of 90 days or less, bail bonds or binary options.
rules.rewrite: Remove the product. Longer-term loans may be allowed under the Credit special category.

rules.title: Landing page is not https
rules.explain: Pages without https look unsafe, and browsers may warn people away.
rules.rewrite: Use the https:// version of the link.

rules.title: Landing page link is still a placeholder
rules.explain: The link must go to a working page that matches the ad. A placeholder link gets the ad rejected.
rules.rewrite: Put the real page address in the link field.

specialCategories.title: Looks like a housing offer
patterns: \b((apartments?|condos?|homes?|houses?|flats?|villas?|rooms?|propert(y|ies)|townhouses?)\s+(for (rent|sale|lease)|to (rent|let))|for rent|for lease|real estate|realtors?|mortgages?|home loans?|homebuyers?|first[- ]time buyers?|\d+[- ]?(bed(room)?s?|br)|open house|property listings?)\b
specialCategories.explain: Housing ads (homes for sale or rent, mortgages, real estate) must be declared as the Housing special ad category, which limits targeting.
specialCategories.rewrite: When you create the campaign, set special_ad_categories to ["HOUSING"]. Keep the copy the same.

specialCategories.title: Looks like a job offer
patterns: \b(we'?re hiring|now hiring|hiring now|job (openings?|opportunit(y|ies)|vacanc(y|ies)|fair)|vacanc(y|ies)|join our team|apply (now )?for (the|this|our) (role|position|job)|open (roles?|positions?)|careers? at|recruiting|internships?|(full|part)[- ]time (role|position|job)|salary)\b
specialCategories.explain: Job ads must be declared as the Employment special ad category, which limits targeting.
specialCategories.rewrite: When you create the campaign, set special_ad_categories to ["EMPLOYMENT"].

specialCategories.title: Looks like a credit or financing offer
patterns: \b(credit cards?|personal loans?|business loans?|car loans?|auto loans?|student loans?|loans?|line of credit|financing available|0% (apr|interest|financing)|buy now,? pay later|bnpl|pay in \d+ (installments|instalments)|low apr)\b
specialCategories.explain: Credit and financing offers must be declared as the Financial products and services special ad category (older accounts call it Credit), which limits targeting.
specialCategories.rewrite: When you create the campaign, set special_ad_categories to ["FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES"] (or ["CREDIT"] on older API versions).

specialCategories.title: Looks like a political or social issue ad
specialCategories.explain: Ads about elections, politics or social issues need ad account authorization, a "Paid for by" label and the Social issues, elections or politics category.
specialCategories.rewrite: Complete Meta's ad authorization, then set special_ad_categories to ["ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS"].
